projectTone: Polished SaaS marketing and help-center copy for a privacy-aware Mac app. Prefer natural target-language phrasing over literal word order.

doNotLiteralize.meaning: An AI assistant that supports the user during live work. Translate as a natural assistant/helper phrase if a literal aviation metaphor sounds odd.
Designed to keep work on the user's device by default. Translate the concept, not the English compound.
The apparent advertised price. Use a natural phrase for surface price or listed price.
A privacy/security operating mode or stance. Do not translate as physical body posture.
A practice run or rehearsal. Use the local idiom for trial run.
A model, transcription, or service provider. Use the normal technology/business term in the target language.
Real-time assistance during a call, interview, or meeting. Do not imply customer support chat unless the context says that.
The user's sequence of work steps in the app. Translate naturally for product UX copy.
How the conversation feels and behaves when participants know a tool or bot has joined. Paraphrase naturally.
A backup path used when the preferred path is unavailable. Avoid awkward literal fallback imagery.

reviewRubric.meaningScore: 5 means all product/legal/privacy meaning is preserved; 4 means minor wording changes only; 3 or lower fails.
reviewRubric.fluencyScore: 5 means native-quality product copy; 4 means natural and professional; 3 or lower sounds literal, awkward, or machine-translated.
reviewRubric.literalnessRisk: 1 means no literalness risk; 2 acceptable; 3 or higher fails and needs repair.
